human_reference.source: Hebart et al. 2020, THINGS odd-one-out similarity

question: Would learning 20,000-50,000 object names be enough for human-like recognition?
answer: Not with this encoder. A space using ~4 effective dimensions cannot hold tens of thousands of distinguishable clusters; it holds tens. The measured behaviour matches: six classes at 0.789 precision with 45% coverage, and building vs vegetation colliding at cosine 0.841.
diagnosis: The training objective does not demand dimensionality. Triplet loss on same-track vs different-track is satisfiable in very few dimensions, so the encoder never had a reason to use the 32 it was given.
target: Raise effective dimensionality from 3.9 toward the human 49-66. That is now the named constraint on vocabulary size, and it is measurable by participation ratio on any encoder.
note: Vocabulary is cheap once the space is good: naming costs 3-5 anchors per class, so 30,000 classes is ~100k anchor patches. The gate is the space, not the word count.
